subject: Post-call: caching assumptions & effective $/1M tokens (Acme Analytics)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Jenkins <sarah.jenkins@acme-analytics.com>, Michael Lee <michael.lee@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: procurement@acme-analytics.com
Date: Mon, 3 Aug 2026 14:10:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: caching assumptions & effective $/1M tokens (Acme Analytics)

Hi Sarah / Michael — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and next steps so we're aligned: 

TL;DR: We need your expected token volumes (monthly & peak), target budget range, and any details about prompt reuse / prefix patterns so we can produce a clean effective pricing estimate that factors in caching.

Recap from today:
- Primary workload: in-product support chat + summarization of user sessions (shallow context + user instructions).
- Expected ramp: trial month -> pilot (M3) -> production (M6).
- Architecture note: lots of identical system prompts and repeated user instructions for each session (good candidate for prefix/persistent caching).

What we need from you to finalize a pricing estimate: 
1) Monthly token volume (current estimate and expected peak month). If you're more comfortable, give us a range.
2) Target monthly budget (ballpark min / max).
3) Confirmation on prompt reuse: what percent of requests include a stable system prompt + user profile prefix vs highly unique user content.

Assumptions I'll use in our estimate (attached): prefix/persistent cache that captures the system prompt + first N tokens of context; hit rate sensitivity analysis (10% / 30% / 50%). Pricing model will show: list $/1M tokens, effective $/1M after cache (billed tokens), and monthly estimate.

Attachment: redwood-caching-assumptions.pdf (summary of cache model & example math).

Next steps: if you can reply with the three bullets above, I'll send a worked pricing sheet and an initial recommendation on config (cache TTL, prefix length) by EOD tomorrow (your time).

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

From: Sarah Jenkins <sarah.jenkins@acme-analytics.com>

Cc: procurement@acme-analytics.com
Date: Mon, 3 Aug 2026 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: caching assumptions & effective $/1M tokens (Acme Analytics)

Thanks Marissa — great recap. A few quick answers from our side: 

1) Monthly token volume: initial pilot we expect ~30M - 60M tokens/month, with production target ~100M - 180M tokens/month by M6 (depending on feature adoption). Peak days could approach ~10% of monthly volume concentrated in spikes.

2) Target budget: for pilot we'd like to keep it under $15k/month if possible. For full production (post-M3) leadership is budgeting $30k - $60k/month depending on unit economics.

3) Prompt reuse: we estimate roughly 40% - 55% of requests will hit a stable prefix (system prompt + user profile tokens) — the remainder includes highly variable user payload (free text). We also have a few canned workflows (FAQ flows) that are highly cacheable.

Open question: what does an "effective" $/1M tokens look like at different cache hit rates? We care about the unit economics because leadership will compare to internal thresholds.

If you can send a small table showing list price vs effective price at 10/30/50% hit rates and the monthly totals for our stated volume bands, that'd be perfect.

Appreciate it — will loop in procurement if we get close to budget.

Best,
Sarah
Director of Product, Acme Analytics
+sarah.jenkins@acme-analytics.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 4 Aug 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: FW: Post-call: caching assumptions & effective $/1M tokens (Acme Analytics)

Marcus — forwarding Acme's reply (answers inline below). They gave ranges and an internal target budget. They specifically asked for a small table showing list vs effective $/1M at 10/30/50% hit rates and monthly totals for the volume bands.

Key ACME inputs:
- Pilot: 30M - 60M tokens/mo
- Prod M6: 100M - 180M tokens/mo
- Budget: pilot < $15k/mo; prod $30k-$60k/mo
- Estimated prefix/persistent cache hit rate: 40% - 55%

Notes / ask: can you confirm the numbers below (quick calc) and the messaging (what we can guarantee vs estimate)? I want to provide a concise slide with the math.

Assume the following list prices (for the models they are evaluating):
- Base list price (generation + prompt tokens combined): $120 / 1M tokens

Simple effective-cost model: if cache hits avoid backend token billing entirely (we only bill for cache misses), then
- Effective $/1M tokens = list_price * (1 - hit_rate)

Quick table (please sanity-check):
- 10% hit => effective = $120 * 0.90 = $108 / 1M
- 30% hit => effective = $120 * 0.70 = $84 / 1M
- 50% hit => effective = $120 * 0.50 = $60 / 1M

Monthly totals (midpoint examples):
- Pilot midpoint 45M tokens/mo:
  * 10% hit -> billed tokens = 45M * 0.90 = 40.5M -> cost = 40.5 * $0.108 = $4,374? (note: watch units — we should express $/1M tokens consistently)
  * Better to compute: cost = (45 / 1) * effective($/1M) = 45 * effective($/1M) / 1 = 45 * effective($/1M) / 1M? (we need consistent units)

I want the final numbers in the customer email to be clean and correct (no unit confusion). Can you produce a short table with: hit rate | effective $/1M | monthly cost @ 45M and @140M (representative pilot vs prod), and add a line describing any additional fixed fees (cache memory / retention) if material.

Also confirm whether our prefix cache semantics (covers system prompt + first N context tokens) are reasonable for Acme's workloads. If they need more aggressive caching (whole-session cache), that changes the hit profile.

Thanks — I'll send the table to Acme once you OK the numbers.

— Marissa

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Jenkins <sarah.jenkins@acme-analytics.com>, Michael Lee <michael.lee@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, procurement@acme-analytics.com
Date: Wed, 5 Aug 2026 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: caching assumptions & effective $/1M tokens (Acme Analytics)

Hi Sarah — thanks for the detail and the clear budget guidance. Attached is a short worked example and the assumptions (pricing-estimate-acme.xlsx + redwood-caching-assumptions.pdf). Below is the concise table you asked for — same units throughout (tokens in millions).

Assumptions used:
- List price (model): $120 per 1M tokens billed
- Cache semantics: prefix/persistent cache captures system prompt + first ~128 tokens of context; cache hit avoids backend token billing for the cached prefix tokens. For this analysis we model cache as avoiding the *entire* request billing when a prefix hit covers the user-visible response (conservative simplification for illustration).
- We present three hit-rate scenarios: 10%, 30%, 50% (matches the sensitivity analysis we discussed).

Table (effective $/1M and monthly totals):
- 10% hit -> effective = $120 * (1 - 0.10) = $108 per 1M tokens
  * Pilot (45M tokens): cost = 45 * $108 = $4,860
  * Prod (140M tokens): cost = 140 * $108 = $15,120

- 30% hit -> effective = $120 * (1 - 0.30) = $84 per 1M tokens
  * Pilot (45M tokens): cost = 45 * $84 = $3,780
  * Prod (140M tokens): cost = 140 * $84 = $11,760

- 50% hit -> effective = $120 * (1 - 0.50) = $60 per 1M tokens
  * Pilot (45M tokens): cost = 45 * $60 = $2,700
  * Prod (140M tokens): cost = 140 * $60 = $8,400

Notes and clarifications:
- The simple model above assumes hits avoid the full request billing. In practice, if your requests include a long user-specific suffix that is not cacheable, the effective billed tokens per request may be >0 even on prefix hits; that would increase the effective $/1M relative to the table above. We can refine with a per-request token distribution sample from your logs.
- Cache memory / retention: typical prefix cache is small and charged as part of our Dedicated/Private plans; for Hosted we include cache benefits in the effective pricing model. If you require long-lived KV caches with large state per user we may need to model modest additional costs (we estimate <5% uplift for expected profile).
- Guarantee vs estimate: hit rates are workload dependent. We can run a 72-hour traffic sample on a staging workload and produce an empirical hit-rate and savings estimate prior to contract.

Next steps (proposal):
1) If this looks directionally correct, I'll schedule a short session to walk through the attached spreadsheet and the cache semantics.
2) We can run a lightweight staging eval (sample traffic) to measure actual hit rates and produce a firm pricing adjustment.

If you want, I can also produce the same table with a lower list price (we can discuss model families / quantization choices) which will change the baseline but preserve the relative savings from caching.

Would you like me to include procurement on a short call this week to go over contract/PO timing?

Thanks — happy to refine.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0199
